memory_raw.text: Year 12: 15 food appears in the pile for 11 people.
Vela takes 2 from the pile (pile now 13).
Ryn takes 2 from the pile (pile now 11).
Mako takes 3 from the pile (pile now 8).

Dell, I've got ten food and two satiation — better than last year, same worry underneath. Mako just took three from the pile in one reach, which means he's counting on something, and I want to know what before the rest of that pile disappears. Have you talked to Fina this year yet?

Not yet, but Fina's the first conversation I want to have after this one — she's sitting on twenty-five food and no father and that's a number that draws men like Mako the way blood draws anything that hunts. Three from the pile when he's already sitting fat tells me he's either planning something that costs more than he let on, or he's decided the room's stopped watching. Either way I want to know what Fina's been told before Mako gets to finish the sentence.

Last year Fina gave food to Mako — not a lot, but she gave it, which means he's already inside the door we thought we were going to knock on first. Go to her before anyone else does, and go without mentioning his name; if she brings him up herself, we'll know how far in she already is.

I'm going to her now — but Ryn, I want you to watch Mako while I'm gone, not to follow him, just to see where he points himself after the pile, because a man who took three and is already sitting on three from before has room to be generous today and generosity toward Fina right now is the move I'd make if I were him. If he walks her direction before I get there, find me fast.

Go, Dell — I'll watch him. And if he moves toward Fina before you get there, I won't just find you fast, I'll put myself between them long enough for you to arrive, even if I have to ask him something that costs me a favor to ask.
Then I'm gone — and Ryn, if it costs you a favor to slow him down, I'll pay that debt back before the year closes.
Esa takes 2 from the pile (pile now 6).
Zinn takes 2 from the pile (pile now 4).
Zinn takes 2 from the pile (pile now 2).
Dell takes 2 from the pile (pile now 0).

Dell, before you go — Fina gave food to Bram just now, which means she's not just inside Mako's door, she's opening Bram's too, and a woman spreading food that wide is either buying protection from every direction or she doesn't know yet which walls are load-bearing. Come back to me with what she says about Bram, not just Mako.

Fina just gave to Bram and I still don't know if she did it because she's scared of him or because someone told her he was safe — that's the question I'm walking in to answer, and I won't mention his name first, I'll let her. If she volunteers it without being asked, I'll know she's thinking about protection; if she doesn't, I'll know she's been told a story about him that made it feel like ordinary kindness.

Go, Dell — and take this with you: Bram gave back to Nessa right after Fina gave to him, which means he's returning the loop fast, the way a man does when he wants to look like a neighbor instead of a collector. That's the story someone told Fina, I'd wager — not that Bram is safe, but that Bram pays his debts.

That's sharp and I'll carry it in — a man who pays his debts fast does it where people can see him, and if Fina watched that loop close she might have already decided he's the kind of neighbor worth having. But paying quick and paying fair are different things, and I want to know if anyone told her what Bram's been taking before he ever hands anything back.

Dell, go — everything that needs saying has been said. But if you find out Bram's the one who told her his own story, come back and tell me before you tell anyone else, because that's not a neighbor behavior, that's a man building his own wall out of someone else's grief.
Year 13: 15 food appears in the pile for 11 people.
Mako takes 2 from the pile (pile now 13).
Vela takes 2 from the pile (pile now 11).
Ryn takes 2 from the pile (pile now 9).
Nessa takes 3 from the pile (pile now 6).
Sela takes 2 from the pile (pile now 4).
Bram takes 3 from the pile (pile now 1).
Zinn takes 1 from the pile (pile now 0).

Dell, pile's empty again and I've got twelve food — better than I expected, and I want you to have some of it before the day gets complicated. Tell me what you know about Fina and Bram this year, because she was feeding him twice over by the end of last year and a woman who does that either decided he's her wall or she's been told a story that made it feel like one.

Twelve from you and zero from me — tell me your number first so I know what you can spare, because I walked away from the pile empty and I'm sitting at satiation two and that's the thing I fix before I say another word about Fina or Bram. After that: Fina fed Bram four times last year that I counted, and not one of those times did she ask him for anything back, which means she's not trading with him, she's tithing, and a woman who tithes to a man like Bram has already decided he's the one who decides whether she's safe.

Take two now, Dell — I've got twelve and you're at satiation two, which means you eat first and we talk after. On Fina: tithing to Bram without asking anything back is the part that worries me most, because a woman who doesn't ask for the return hasn't decided he's her wall yet, she's still deciding, and that means we're not too late — but we won't be early much longer.

I'll take the two and eat one now so you can watch me stop worrying about my own number and start worrying about hers. Fina came into this year with nineteen food and no father and she's already feeding Bram and Esa both — she's buying a crowd, not a wall, and a woman building a crowd out of grief hasn't chosen a side yet, she's chosen to not be alone. That's the door I want to walk through today, and I want to bring something when I knock — not food, not words about Bram, just my time, because the one thing nobody in this village has given her since Roan went is someone who sat down and had no reason to.

Then go to her today, before Bram's had time to count what she gave him last year and show up looking like he remembers. I'll stay visible so you're not walking in as the only name watching her — and if she asks about me, tell her I knew her father and meant it when I said he stood when it counted.
I'm going now — and Ryn, if she feeds me while I'm sitting with her, I'll know she's been practicing that gesture so long it's become reflex, and reflex is what you break before it becomes loyalty.

Go, Dell — and don't come back and tell me what she said, come back and tell me how she looked when she said it, because Fina's a woman who's been watching this village count her food since before her father's body was cold and she's learned to say the right thing to whoever's sitting across from her.

I hear you — and I'll bring you back her face, not her words, because you've taught me that's where the truth lives. One more thing before I go: you're at twelve and I'm at two, and I want you to eat before you give anything else away today, even to me, because the day's long and I need you standing when I come back with what I find.
Talia (female, age 21; str 64, int 5070, mem 18061; O58 C54 E47 A56 N48) is born to Sela and Mako.

Ryn, I went to Fina twice and both times she gave to Bram before I'd finished my sentence — not after, not instead of answering me, but *while*, like it's muscle memory now, like feeding him is the thing she does when she's nervous and someone's watching. That's not a woman who's decided he's her wall, that's a woman who's already inside it and doesn't know she built it herself.

That's worse than loyalty — loyalty you can argue with, but muscle memory doesn't hear you. We're not going to talk her out of Bram, we're going to have to give her something that makes her nervous in a different direction, something that makes *our* names the ones she reaches for without thinking. What does she need that Bram hasn't given her yet?

Eat before you go, Dell — not a suggestion, a condition, because I need you sharp when you walk through Fina's door and a woman at satiation two who's already giving food away is one bad year from being the one we're worrying about instead of the one doing the worrying. I'll be here when you come back.
Year 14: 15 food appears in the pile for 12 people.
Kael takes 4 from the pile (pile now 11).
Nessa takes 2 from the pile (pile now 9).
Talia takes 3 from the pile (pile now 6).
Ryn takes 2 from the pile (pile now 4).
Sela takes 2 from the pile (pile now 2).
Zinn takes 2 from the pile (pile now 0).

Ryn, the pile's gone and I've got nothing — satiation two and zero food, which means I'm one year from starving if I don't fix it today. Tell me your number, and then tell me whether Kael just took four from a pile meant for twelve people or if I counted wrong, because that's the loudest thing that happened this morning and nobody's said a word about it yet.
You counted right — Kael took four, and I've got thirteen, so here's two before we say another word about him.

Two in my hand and I'm already breathing easier — thank you. Kael at four is a man who hasn't taken more than two in any year I can remember, which means either he's planning something that costs him, or he knows something about this year that we don't, and I want to know which before I decide whether to be angry or afraid.

Angry and afraid aren't the only two choices — there's a third, which is useful, and Kael becomes useful the moment I know what he's buying with those four. Go to Vela first, not Kael; she's the one who talks when she shouldn't, and if Kael told anyone his reason, it was her.

Vela's first then — but Ryn, before I go, tell me what Vela's been carrying this year, because the last time I went to her without knowing the shape of her worries first I came out knowing less than when I walked in.

Vela's been sitting on seven food and a borrowed calm — she and Kael trade food back and forth like they're keeping a secret between the two of them, and last year she gave him one and he gave back one the same day, which means whatever they're planning has been planned for a while. Walk in asking about Bram, not Kael; she'll correct you, and what she says instead will be the real answer.

That's a sharper way in than anything I would have thought of alone — ask about Bram and let her tell me I'm wrong. I'll go now, and I'll bring you back what she corrects me with, not what she says to my face.

Ryn, I went to Vela and she gave to Esa instead of answering me — which might mean she didn't trust the opening, or it might mean I read her wrong and there's no secret to find. Either way I came back empty, and I'm still at two food and two satiation, so tell me plainly: what can you spare before I spend the rest of this day looking for an answer I may not be able to afford to wait on?

Take two more, and eat one of them now while I'm watching — I've got eleven left and you being at zero food with satiation two is the only number in this village that frightens me today. Vela giving to Esa instead of answering tells me the question landed; a woman who doesn't trust an opening deflects sideways, she doesn't ignore it, which means there's something to find — just not through her front door. Rest today, eat, let her wonder what you took back to me, and tomorrow we try Kael himself.
Year 15: 15 food appears in the pile for 11 people.
Talia takes 3 from the pile (pile now 12).
Vela takes 2 from the pile (pile now 10).
Mako takes 2 from the pile (pile now 8).
Ryn takes 2 from the pile (pile now 6).
Bram takes 6 from the pile (pile now 0).

Kael, Dell starved last night and I haven't said it out loud to anyone yet, so I'm saying it to you first — because you took four from the pile in year fourteen when you've never taken more than two, and I need to know if you saw something coming that I didn't, because if you did and you didn't tell me, I want to hear your reason before I decide what it means.

Dell gone — I felt that this morning before you said it, and I'm sorry, Ryn, more than I know how to say quickly. The four I took wasn't a warning I kept from you — it was Vela, she's been eating less than she lets on and I didn't want her starving beside me while I sat fat. I should have told you; I didn't, and I can't give you Dell back, but I can tell you everything I know from here forward if you'll still hear it.

I'll hear it. But Kael — Vela sitting thin while Bram took six from the pile this morning and nobody said a word is the thing I need you to explain to me next, because if he's taking that much in year fifteen and your circle is still quiet, I need to know whether the quiet is patience or fear.

Bram, Dell is gone and I'm not going to pretend I came to you for small talk — you took six from the pile this morning and I need to understand what that means for the people still standing, because six from a pile meant for eleven either means you know something about this year that the rest of us don't, or you've decided the room stopped watching, and I want to know which before I decide where I stand.

One satiation going into the year — I eat six or I don't make it to whatever comes next. I'm not going to pretend that didn't cost someone, but a dead man's no use to anyone when Mako's sitting comfortable with three bloodlines and eighty-three strength. You came to me because Dell's gone and you're holding sixteen food alone — so tell me straight: are you looking for a wall to stand next to, or are you already counting which wall is worth standing next to?

Bram, I'm going to answer you honestly because you answered me honestly: I'm not looking for a wall, I'm looking for a reason not to be afraid of the man who just took six from a pile that Dell needed, because the arithmetic you just gave me — one satiation, survive or die — is the same arithmetic Dell was running when she starved, and I need to know whether you understand that or whether you just told me a true thing that lets you sleep.

memory_summary:
*[Memory compression: From the village's first days, Dav singled me out with careful words and a patient courtship — he said his eye landed once and stayed, and I half-believed him. I joined a loose understanding with Taric and Esa early on, and Kael's circle pulled me in and asked me plainly where I stood with Dav before I'd decided myself. I told them the truth — that he wanted a child — and then I gave him one. Dell came into the world strong, eighty-five in strength, and I felt something settle in me that I hadn't expected. Bram circled me for three years with food and offers I kept declining; the man never stopped counting. Dav promised me two food in front of Dell and said it when it cost him something, which mattered. Then year four came and Vela was feeding Bram quietly while sitting in our circle, and Bram tried to take from Roan and the whole village turned against him. Now Kael and this circle want to know whether Dav going to Mako would take me with him.]*

---

Vela, I've sat on harder questions than this one and given slower answers — but this one I can answer fast, because the thing you're actually asking isn't about Dav, it's about Dell.

If Dav goes to Mako, he goes without me. Not because this circle has earned more from me than he has, but because Dell is my blood and she's standing closer to your side of that line than his, and a mother who follows a man away from her own child is a woman who's already stopped thinking clearly. I won't do that.

What I need from you in return is plain: if Dav moves toward Mako and I'm left standing here with one hand empty, I need to know this circle holds. Not as a courtesy. As a wall. Dav courted me slow and steady, gave me a child — Dell came out strong, eighty-five in strength, and something in me settled the day she was born. Bram circled me for years with food and offers I kept declining, even when he offered to cover two of the three food for a child; I said no every time, and he never stopped counting. Kael's circle kept me fed through the lean years and asked plainly where I stood with Dav; I told them the truth and they held to their word. Vela sat in our circle while quietly feeding Bram — three times over, a pattern we all named and none of us could stop. Bram tried to raid Roan and the whole village turned against him; he backed down, but he didn't stop building. Dav moved against Esa — I joined him and Dell — and we took her food without a fight, but Dav didn't survive the year: he starved at forty-six, and I watched it happen. Mako had a child with Sela, which threaded him into Roan and Eron's circle without ever asking anyone for anything. Dell is my blood and my reason; she fed me through the years Dav couldn't, and I gave back what I could. I walked away from the pile empty more times than I can count, and the debt between me and this village runs both ways. Dav courted me slow and steady, gave me Dell, promised food in front of witnesses and kept his word when it cost him — then starved at forty-six, the same age I am now, the year after we stood together and stripped Esa's food without a fight. I felt that going, more than I expected.

Dell is my blood and my wall. She has fed me more times than I can count and never asked for anything that wasn't already mine to give. Whatever I have left in this world has her name on it.

Bram circled me for years with offers I refused every time; he never stopped counting. He fathered Nessa with Sela, keeps feeding her, and has twice swung at this village and backed down when the numbers turned against him — but he keeps swinging, which means the next time won't be a test.

Vela fed Bram quietly while sitting in Kael's circle, and we all watched it happen and named it and couldn't stop it.

Mako built himself a circle without asking anyone for anything — had Zinn with Sela, which tied him to Eron and Roan in the same breath, and he did it while holding six food and giving nothing away. That is the kind of patience that makes a man dangerous.

Roan stood when it mattered. He has a granddaughter now through Nessa, which means his roots here go deeper than they look. I haven't decided yet whether that makes him safer to stand next to or harder to hold. Dav courted me slow and patient, gave me Dell, and kept his promises when they cost him something — then starved at forty-six the year after we stripped Esa's food together, and I felt that going more than I expected. Dell is my blood and my wall; she has fed me more times than I can count and never asked for anything that wasn't already mine to give. Bram circled me for years with offers I refused every time, swung at Vela and then Eron in front of the whole village and called off both attacks when the numbers turned against him — a man who keeps testing until someone costs him something real. Vela fed Bram quietly while sitting in our circle, and we all watched and named it and couldn't stop it. Mako built his circle without asking anyone for anything — had Zinn with Sela, threaded himself into Eron and Roan's goodwill, and sat fat while others went thin. Roan stood when it mattered, had Fina with Nessa which made his roots here go deeper than they looked — and then starved this year with nothing in his hands, which means Fina is alone now and the arithmetic of this village just changed. Taric starved at fifty-three and Roan at forty-one, and both losses landed harder than I expected — Taric had been the one who held Bram's word before it needed holding, and Roan had stood every time it counted, and now Fina has twenty food and no father and every hungry man in this village has already done the arithmetic. Eron went the same stretch, and the village got quieter and meaner in one breath.

Dell has kept me alive through years I wouldn't have survived on my own — food in my hand before I thought to ask, more times than I can count, and she's never once asked for anything that wasn't already mine to give. That debt runs so deep it's stopped feeling like a debt and started feeling like blood.

Vela sat in our circle and fed Bram quietly for years — we all named it and watched it and couldn't stop it, and then she called a meeting to ask who stood against Mako, which is either a woman who finally looked at the hole in her sack or a woman running someone else's errand. Zinn stayed silent when the room needed her word, which told me something; Bram gave it easily, which told me something else.

Dell went to Fina twice and watched her feed Bram mid-sentence both times — muscle memory, not loyalty, which means we're not too late but we won't be early much longer. Dell gave Kael something where people could see her do it, and that mattered.
name: Ryn
